prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web app direction comp, 1440 by 900 landscape canvas
Primary request: Create a shippable SafeDay consumer utility interface in the visual direction "The Trail Marker". The screen should feel immediately usable, calm, and decisively minimal.
Scene/backdrop: A quiet matte field filling the viewport in warm off-white #f1f2ea.
Subject: A slim 64px header containing the SafeDay wordmark and one compact place control. Below it, show one single route-like weather recommendation running horizontally or diagonally through the quiet field, with a restrained painted route line in green #34734d. Present the exact primary copy "Tomorrow", "7:00 to 9:00 AM", and "Best for a walk". Include one plain-language reason for the recommendation. Show these compact real metrics exactly: "24 C", "Rain 1%", "Air 82 AQI", and "UV 1.0". Fold the week into a trail legend rail below the main recommendation, and keep alternative time windows visibly available but secondary.
Style/medium: Polished high-fidelity UI design mockup, minimal consumer weather utility, precise modern typography, generous negative space, disciplined information hierarchy, clean production-ready spacing.
Composition/framing: Full-bleed desktop application screen only, no browser frame. The recommendation route is the clear focal point. Keep controls small and familiar. Alternatives remain visible without competing with the recommended window.
Color palette: Warm off-white #f1f2ea, deep near-black green #17211b, and exactly one green accent #34734d.
Materials/textures: Subtle matte enamel trailhead sign material and one painted route line, interpreted abstractly and digitally, not literal park-sign cosplay.
Text (verbatim): "SafeDay"; "Tomorrow"; "7:00 to 9:00 AM"; "Best for a walk"; "24 C"; "Rain 1%"; "Air 82 AQI"; "UV 1.0". Render all required text exactly with no misspellings and no extra punctuation.
Constraints: Relatable and immediately usable. One clear recommendation, one plain-language reason, compact metrics, a week trail legend rail, and visible alternatives. Strong accessibility through contrast, readable type, and clear hierarchy.
Avoid: card grid, gradients, multicolor weather cards, fake browser chrome, huge buttons, giant Privacy button, extra form fields, literal national park signage, hand-drawn icon cluster, decorative dots, em dash, en dash, visual clutter, glossy effects, skeuomorphic wood, badges, illustrations, photos, and watermarks.
